brief: A two-storey white-painted clapboard corner store: flat roof, shop windows with a striped awning on the ground floor, a painted mural of a ship on the side wall, street lamps and a parked van. One photo. Older than 1970: Lake Erie island and harbour-town main streets (the Put-in-Bay model) are 19th-century commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: Hart's Drug Store (Vermilion OH, 1870s): a two-storey side-gabled painted-brick building on a corner with a soda grill's traditional storefront, a striped awning, a transom of small panes, a mural of the town on the side wall, flag bunting; decorative lamps and hanging baskets

why.note: a revitalised lake town: murals and bunting (Main Street program)
